title: Chapter 145: We Are All Monsters (2)
html:
Wang Shenglong’s father watched the visitors from the corner of his eye. He knew his son’s appearance drew stares, and every judgmental glance caused him indescribable pain. This time, however, both Doctor Gao and Chen Ge behaved naturally.

“Exercise can reduce cardiac risk and relieve stress. Try not to keep him confined at home.” Doctor Gao removed his shoes and sat beside Wang Shenglong without disgust or condescension. Far from fearing him, Shenglong seemed to welcome the company.

He shifted his large body with difficulty, doing his best to welcome the doctor. Their interaction remained peaceful until Chen Ge entered.

The moment Chen Ge stepped into the bedroom, Wang Shenglong’s smile vanished. His expression hardened, and he glared like a lion sensing another predator inside its territory.

Seated beside him, Doctor Gao noticed the change immediately and looked toward Chen Ge in confusion. Chen Ge also recognized that Shenglong’s reaction was abnormal.

What did he sense? The cat’s scent, or Zhang Ya’s presence?Chen Ge stopped and sat farther away.

“Perhaps so many strangers unsettled him.” Doctor Gao defused the tension by beginning an ordinary conversation. He avoided any mention of mental illness and spoke as though to a friend. Wang Shenglong gradually relaxed and answered on his writing board.

Chen Ge listened in silence. Doctor Gao’s tactful small talk quietly drew out Shenglong’s childhood trauma, daily habits, and history with doctors.

After forty minutes, Doctor Gao increasingly doubted that Shenglong suffered from a psychological disorder. His mind was clear, he communicated willingly, and he wanted treatment. Listening nearby, the family felt vindicated. Beneath his unusual appearance, Shenglong was kind and harmless.

Afterward, Doctor Gao drew Shenglong’s father aside. “He behaves normally and shows no obvious psychological disorder. I suspect he is concealing something.”

People with mental illness often appeared ordinary until an episode drove them to behavior others could not understand.

“He has never hurt anyone or behaved strangely. Apart from refusing to speak or exercise, he is normal.” Shenglong’s father brought Doctor Gao a glass of water.

Shenglong had described the childhood nightmare during their conversation. “A normal child suddenly lost his voice. Could his story have been true?”

Wang Shenglong’s father shook his head with a sigh. “We have no idea whether it’s real or not. We’ve seen so many doctors, but none of them could confirm or deny it.”

“Whether it was objectively real matters less than the fact that Shenglong remembers every detail after so many years. The event profoundly affected him. Resolve that trauma, and he may speak again.”

“But if this incident is completely made up, how are we supposed to help him solve it?” Wang Hailong asked.

“Even if fictional, every detail carries real meaning for Shenglong, just as dreams reflect waking life.” Doctor Gao showed them the recording on his phone. “We cannot interpret it only at face value. I can promise nothing yet, but I will do my best.”

“Doctor Gao, as long as you can cure Shenglong…”

“I cannot guarantee success. After years without speech, his language ability may have regressed.” Doctor Gao looked toward the bedroom. “More urgently, his weight places his life in danger.”

“We’ve tried. He hates exercise and refuses to leave the bedroom, even for the living room.” Frustration weighed on his father.

“Keep communicating. Change how he sees the situation, and his behavior may follow.”

While Doctor Gao spoke with the family outside, Chen Ge sat across from Shenglong. The man’s smile had vanished, and the small eyes nearly hidden among folds of flesh narrowed as they studied him.

“Wang Shenglong, I want to help, so stop hiding the truth.” Chen Ge maintained a safe distance. Shenglong distrusted him, while the repellent odor—apparently perceptible only to Chen Ge—made approaching difficult.

Grabbing the board, Wang Shenglong wrote, “I’m not hiding anything; I’ve told you everything.”

“You know whether that’s true.” Chen Ge lowered his voice. “They care about why you stopped speaking. I care about the memory you hate most. What happened inside the Third Sick Hall?”

At the words Third Sick Hall, Shenglong’s face quivered. His heavy hands clenched into fists, and his body began to shake.

“Your fear of doctors began after you left. What happened there?” Chen Ge caught his fists. “You are a normal person threatened by something abnormal. Tell me the truth, and I can help.”

Wang Shenglong rejected the offer. He erupted without warning and hurled Chen Ge away with astonishing force.

Breathing hard, Shenglong glared at him. After a long silence, he wrote on the board.

“We have both become monsters. Worry about yourself, not me.”
